newsitem.title: USA: Station trims staff at Kansas City casino.
newsitem.headline: Station trims staff at Kansas City casino.

text.p: Station Casinos Inc said it dropped 162 employees from the payroll at its month-old Kansas City casino, and a spokesman Tuesday cited layoffs and attrition.

"It's mainly attrition. Some are people who do not want to work in the gaming business after they tried it. Some are layoffs and others are just staff adjustments," Jack Taylor, a Station spokesman, told Reuters.
"Some departments are not as busy as others. We're hiring in other divisions," Taylor said. "It's... a readjustment after the grand opening."

Station's Kansas City casino complex, which opened Jan 16, is the largest gaming operation in the Midwest and the fourth-largest casino in the United States. With the latest job cuts, the operation now employs around 2,940 people.

Kansas City Star newspaper reported earlier Tuesday that the cuts hit all staff levels, but that the casino's entertainment division was hit hard when 37 workers, mostly sound and lighting technicians, were released Saturday.
The Star quoted Joe Canfora, Station's Midwest president, who said the entertainment division was a staff area where the casino "overshot" in its hiring.
He said the layoffs in teh entertainment division came after the casino realized that music groups being booked were bringing their own technicians with them.

The layoffs at Station came days after Boyd Gaming Corp said 39 middle managers had lost their jobs at Sam's Town Casino in Kansas City, one of Station's four other competitors in the Kansas City casino market.
